Assume small-deformation, linear-elastic, homogeneous, isotropic material behavior.
Assume the shaft is a solid circular prismatic bar governed by Saint-Venant torsion, so plane sections remain plane and no warping constraint is required.
Assume the applied torques are concentrated couples about the shaft axis, with no transverse force, no bending, no axial load, and no stress concentration effects.
Use the right-hand-rule sign convention: x increases from the fixed support at x=0 toward x=1200 mm, and a positive torque vector points in the +x direction.
The polar moment of inertia is J = π d^4 / 32.
The torsional shear stress at radius r is τ(r) = T_internal r / J.
The maximum shear stress occurs at r = d/2 and is τ_max = T_internal (d/2) / J.
The angle of twist for a segment is Δφ = T_internal L_segment / (G J), using the same sign convention for T_internal.
The total angle of twist at x = L is the sum of the segment twists.
The reaction torque at the fixed support is zero because T1 + T2 = 0.
The internal torque in the segment 0 ≤ x ≤ 400 mm is 0 N·mm.
The internal torque in the segment 400 mm ≤ x ≤ 1200 mm is +200,000 N·mm under the stated sign convention.
The maximum shear stress in the segment 0 ≤ x ≤ 400 mm is 0 MPa.
The maximum shear stress in the segment 400 mm ≤ x ≤ 1200 mm is approximately 37.73 MPa.
The angle of twist at x = 400 mm is 0 rad.
The angle of twist at x = 1200 mm is approximately 0.02616 rad, which is about 1.499 degrees.
